newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX volatilities aloft, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX volatilities aloft, but off highs.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options continued hovering at lofty levels in the face of a host of event risks, although they were off early highs in cautious U.S. trading, dealers said.
"Everyone who needs to buy options has done so, and the rest is position-cleaning," said a U.S. bank trader.

The Group of Seven (G7) policymakers' meeting next weekend was keeping the market wary of shorting options, as did the ongoing Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting ending Wednesday, the Bundesbank policy council meeting on Thursday and Friday's January U.S. employment report.
One-month dollar/mark implied volatility was quoted at 10.3/10.5 percent, down a quarter point from early highs and a tenth off late Monday levels.
One-month dollar/yen stood at 12.5/12.8 percent, off about 0.2 point from highs but up half a point from Monday, as spot stayed above 122.00 yen and slightly below last week's 122.78-yen high.

Traders said short-dated volatilities had become very expensive lately because of gamma buying linked to event risks. But they were now becoming wary of rapid deflation in those options that often followed the actual events.
Short-dated options have higher gamma values, which give them quicker value acceleration when spot rates gyrate wildly, but are also vulnerable when spot calms down.

"There's no interest for gamma overnight, but Thursday and Friday expiries have certainly got some juice," said Ted Voorhees, senior trader at Deutsche Bank in New York. He added that traders seemed to be largely neutral for Monday expiries, which cover the G7 meeting.
"There's some interest in trying to spread by buying some Mondays and selling some other dates, but there's not just outright buying in Mondays," he said.

"There's not enough concern to make people feel 'I have to have it'," he added. "I don't think many people are going into the weekend short, but I don't think many people are going into the weekend banking on some major news coming out of G7."

Traders said the market was beginning to look beyond the weekend G7 meeting. Few expected a reversal in the dollar's uptrend, but many saw a slowdown of its ascent, which could take a toll on volatilities.
"It (volatility) is off just a little bit, but the fact that it's lower at all in front of these events may be saying there's more to come," Voorhees said.
Risk reversals, which reflect pricing differential between puts and calls, remained skewed for dollar calls.
One-month 25-delta dollar/mark and dollar/yen stood at 0.2/0.5 percent bid for mark puts and 0.4/0.7 percent bid for yen puts.
Elsewhere, sterling volatilities were well bid after a sharp rebound in spot cable in the past two days back above $1.6260 from the $1.5950 area.
One-month cable volatility was at 10.7/11.1 percent, off a quarter point from early highs but up about half a point on the day.
